text:
The mistake almost every Kamakura day-tripper makes?
Big shrine first, then a race to the Great Buddha.
Flip it, and you get both without the rush 👇

👉 One opening time here surprised even us:
https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset

❌ The usual order
Tsurugaoka Hachimangu first,
because it's 10 minutes from the station.
Then lunch and the shopping street.
Suddenly it's 16:00, and Hase's temples
are about to stop letting people in.

✅ The better order
Go straight to Hase on the Enoden.
From October to March, the Great Buddha's
last entry is 16:45. Hasedera's is 16:30.

🌅 The payoff
Hachimangu is open 6:00 to 20:00, every day, free.
Climb its main steps after sunset,
when most of the crowd is on the train home.

📌 Save this order
Hase temples, then sunset at Inamuragasaki,
then Hachimangu and dinner near the station.
Three short Enoden rides: ¥200, ¥200 and ¥220.

👉 The cape where Fuji shows up on windy winter days:
https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset

On day trips, are you an early starter
or a noon starter?
